archetypes.name: admission-contract
archetypes.rationale: Targets the title-prefix admission contract across /design and /implement surfaces where this plan deliberately changes readiness semantics.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the proposed `[DESIGNING]` to `[DESIGNED]` move is reflected consistently across the plan, implementation targets, and admission documentation. Check for plan defects where `/implement` readiness is still described as publish-gated, rename-delta-gated, or dependent on log PR merge state despite the new `ADMISSION_READY` contract. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: scrub-boundary
archetypes.rationale: Focuses on the new scrub-only gate because it changes when potentially sensitive log material is checked relative to operator-visible admission.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the plan’s `--scrub-only` preflight is sufficient and consistently specified before rename, including fail-closed behavior, warning timing, duplicate warning suppression, and absence of PR or push side effects. Look for missing tests or contract drift where scrub failure, scrub violations, or unexpected scrub-only exits could be confused with publish failure or rename failure. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: operator-recovery
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether failed-publish and failed-admission operator guidance matches the new early-admission design instead of stale recovery paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the proposed summary-render and skill-doc updates for operator-experience defects after publish failure, scrub failure, rename failure, and rename no-op. Verify that recovery guidance distinguishes log recovery from admission recovery and does not tell operators to manually rename or rerun the wrong step when `ADMISSION_READY` is already true or scrub failed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
